cards.prompt: What crate-level attribute disables the Rust standard library so code can run on bare-metal microcontrollers without an OS or heap?
cards.explanation: #![no_std] links only against core (and optionally alloc), removing OS-dependent abstractions like std::fs or std::thread.

cards.prompt: What attribute marks the custom entry point function in a bare-metal Rust firmware binary using cortex-m-rt?
cards.explanation: #[entry] requires a diverging function signature fn main() -> ! because bare-metal firmware never returns.

cards.prompt: What does the return type '-> !' signify on a Rust bare-metal main() or panic handler function?
cards.explanation: Enforces at compile time that the firmware loops infinitely or triggers a hardware reset.

cards.prompt: What are Rust's 3 core ownership rules that prevent data races and use-after-free at compile time?
cards.answer: 1) Each value has one owner; 2) Only one owner at a time; 3) Value is dropped when owner goes out of scope
accepted_answers: 1) Each value has one owner; 2) Only one owner at a time; 3) Value is dropped when owner goes out of scope
Each value has a single owner, only one owner at a time, and the value is dropped when the owner leaves scope
cards.explanation: Combined with borrowing rules (many &T OR one &mut T), Rust guarantees memory and thread safety without a garbage collector.

cards.prompt: How does the Rust Type-State pattern prevent configuring a GPIO pin as an output and accidentally calling .is_high() (an input-only method)?
cards.answer: Zero-sized marker types (PhantomData<State>) encode hardware modes in the type signature so invalid methods do not exist on that type
accepted_answers: Zero-sized marker types (PhantomData<State>) encode hardware modes in the type signature so invalid methods do not exist on that type
Encodes pin state in generic type parameters using PhantomData
Uses PhantomData zero-sized types to enforce state transitions at compile time
cards.explanation: Consuming self during mode transitions (into_push_pull_output(self) -> Pin<Output>) makes invalid hardware states unrepresentable at zero runtime cost.

cards.prompt: What are the 4 architectural layers of the Embedded Rust hardware stack from lowest to highest?
cards.answer: PAC (Peripheral Access Crate) -> HAL (Hardware Abstraction Layer) -> embedded-hal Traits -> Board/Application Driver
accepted_answers: PAC (Peripheral Access Crate) -> HAL (Hardware Abstraction Layer) -> embedded-hal Traits -> Board/Application Driver
cards.explanation: PAC is auto-generated from SVD files via svd2rust; HAL adds safe type-state wrappers; embedded-hal provides portable bus traits (SpiDevice, I2c).

cards.prompt: What async embedded Rust framework runs cooperative async/await tasks on bare-metal microcontrollers without heap allocation?
cards.explanation: Embassy compiles async tasks into statically allocated state machines driven directly by hardware interrupts.

cards.prompt: What modern Rust embedded debugging/flashing tool replaces OpenOCD + GDB and streams defmt logs over RTT?
cards.explanation: probe-rs flashes ELF binaries over ST-Link/J-Link and decodes compact defmt log frames on the host PC.

cards.prompt: What Cargo subcommand inspects compiled firmware binaries to break down Flash/RAM usage per crate and function?
cards.explanation: Essential for auditing code size bloat on Flash-constrained Cortex-M microcontrollers.

cards.prompt: In cortex-m bare-metal Rust, what synchronization primitive wraps shared ISR/main data inside a Mutex requiring a CriticalSection token to access?
cards.explanation: Guarantees interrupts are disabled while borrowing the RefCell, preventing concurrent ISR preemption data races.

cards.prompt: Why does defmt ('deferred formatting') dramatically outperform core::fmt::Write on microcontrollers?
cards.answer: String formatting happens on the host PC rather than the MCU; the MCU only transmits compact log indices and raw binary arguments
accepted_answers: String formatting happens on the host PC rather than the MCU; the MCU only transmits compact log indices and raw binary arguments
Formatting is deferred to the host computer
Moves formatting off the microcontroller to the host
cards.explanation: Saves tens of kilobytes of Flash and avoids slow printf formatting inside real-time code.

cards.prompt: What Rust attribute prevents the compiler from mangling a symbol name so C startup code or linker scripts can call it directly?
cards.explanation: Often paired with extern "C" to expose Rust ISR handlers or FFI functions to C toolchains.
